error: Labeling generation failed after 3 requests: CHANGES REQUIRED: has_matching_key uses max(..., default=...) via the keyword `default`, but only the listed builtins and API surface are allowed and `default` keyword arguments on max are not part of the documented runtime API — worse, in key_found/target_room_entered the fallback `default=env.agent_pos[1]` invents a layout fact and, when no ball is on the grid, derives the door row from the agent's position, which can misidentify the locked door. Also, has_matching_key matches the key color by scanning only column env.width - 6 for a door; in most layouts another (unlocked) door shares the locked door's color and the column scan may pick the wrong door's color, so the key color must come from the door at the locked door's position that starts locked, found by place (left wall of the target room), not by color of any door in that column. Additionally, target_door_open only checks is_open at the locked column; a door found open there could be correct, but the row computation shares the same invalid default fallback. Fix: compute the target room row by locating the unique ball in the grid (the mission target lies in a right-column room, so restrict the ball search to right-column rooms), then use that room's row block (row_start = room_row // 5 * 5 … +6) for the locked door and room-entry checks without any default fallback to the agent position, and require in has_matching_key that the carried key's color equals the color of the door at (env.width - 6, door cell) in that room's left wall.
